meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-10 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Horizon CTO), Priya Nair (Eng Mgr), Marco Silva (Backend Lead)
summary: Discovery call to map integration path for Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private) focusing on SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy setup, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating latency and throughput tradeoffs and has compliance needs (SSO, audit logs). Agreed next steps: share pricing comparison, LangChain sample + micro-benchmark, and schedule POC kickoff.
topics: SDKs (official SDKs + LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters), gateway/proxy and network egress, rate limiting and quota model, observability hooks (trace/span, token-level cost breakdown), Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs, security and compliance concerns (SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS), rollout and canary strategy
transcript: 00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call - Maya and Ethan from Redwood. 00:08 Alex (Horizon CTO): Alex here, Priya and Marco are with me. thanks. 00:14 Ethan (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda - integration surface, SDKs, rate limits, observability hooks, and then next steps. 00:25 Priya (Eng Mgr): Sounds good, we're mainly figuring out how Redwood would sit behind our gateway and how people will call it via LangChain. 00:38 Marco (Backend): Also curious about proxies - we currently run an API gateway w/ JWT auth and some per-tenant rate limits.
transcript_continued: 01:05 Maya: Perfect. quick high-level: Hosted is easy for POC and fast time-to-value, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable latency, Private is for VPC / on-prem for compliance. 01:22 Alex: Do you have an official SDK? we use node and python, and our pipeline uses LangChain + a lot of LlamaIndex. 01:35 Ethan: Yes, SDKs for node/python, and we maintain adapter examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex - we'll share the repo. our LangChain connector supports streaming and function-calling. 01:50 Priya: streaming is important for UX. how do you handle streaming through proxies? some of our edge proxies close idle connections quickly. 02:06 Ethan: We do server-sent events and also a websocket option for dedicated/private. for hosted you can use streaming over SSE; if your proxy times out you can use our gateway-proxy pattern or long-lived websocket via Dedicated. 02:23 Marco: Gateway-proxy pattern? can you explain quickly. 02:28 Maya: Sure, you can run a small proxy in your VPC that forwards auth and handles rate limiting locally, while calling Redwood backend or Dedicated endpoint. avoids exposing internal IPs and gives you control over throttling. 02:45 Alex: ok makes sense. what about rate limits and quotas - we have bursty traffic sometimes with spikes to 1k rps on short windows. 02:58 Ethan: We support per-key quotas and per-route rate limits, and Dedicated can be configured with higher throughput and autoscaling policies. for hosted we recommend token quotas + soft caps and request-level rejection callbacks. 03:15 Priya: Do you apply per-user or per-tenant limits? we need per-tenant isolation. 03:21 Ethan: You can do both; typical pattern is per-API-key per-tenant mapping, and Dedicated gives you stronger isolation with reserved pools. 03:32 Alex: How about observability - we need traces, token-level cost breakdown, and per-prompt latency histograms. 03:41 Maya: Redwood Console surfaces token cost and latency by route/model; you can also send tracing hooks and integrate with our tracing API to attach spans to your traces. 03:54 Marco: does that require vendor tracing? we use Datadog and Lightstep. 04:00 Ethan: We export OpenTelemetry-compatible traces and logs so it's straightforward to hook into Datadog/Lightstep. 04:09 Alex: security checklist - SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS for encryption at rest? 04:17 Maya: Yes, we support SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning for enterprise, RBAC policies, audit logs in Console. for key management, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS/HSM. hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed KMS. 04:33 Priya: Any compliance attestations? SOC 2? 04:36 Maya: We're SOC 2 compliant and have ISO in process, we can share our security pack and questionnaire. 04:44 Alex: Good. on the SDK front - does the LangChain adapter keep the chat history on your side or is it up to the client? 04:53 Ethan: The adapter streams tokens and also supports prefix/KV cache options. by default we don't persist customer prompts beyond retention policy - you can enable prefix caching for latency improvements. 05:08 Marco: LlamaIndex - any extra work needed? 05:12 Ethan: We have a LlamaIndex helper and an example notebook that shows indexing + retrieval + Redwood generation. small code change to point the retriever to our embeddings or you can bring your own embedding model. 05:26 Priya: embeddings cost model? we do a lot of vector searches. 05:30 Maya: We price embeddings separately, per-embedding unit; we'll include current pricing bands in the deck. 05:38 Alex: For POC we'd probably start hosted and move to Dedicated if latency or isolation demands it. 05:44 Maya: That's a common path. for POC we can give free test credits and a recommended config for LangChain tests. 05:52 Alex: Are there fallback policies if a model is saturated? we sometimes need graceful degradation. 05:59 Ethan: Yes, Smart routing allows fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost models, and you can configure automatic fallback rules in your rollout policy. 06:12 Marco: any limitations on context length with kv cache and quantized models? 06:17 Ethan: longest context varies by model; we recommend Dedicated for very long contexts > 16k because of memory constraints; quantization can affect performance but we have quantization profiles we can recommend. 06:33 Priya: network egress and data residency - we have EU customers so data can't leave region. 06:39 Maya: We support region pinning on Dedicated/Private; hosted has EU regions as well and options for data residency. 06:47 Alex: latency targets - we typically need 100-200ms at 512 tokens for autocomplete paths. can Redwood hit that? 06:56 Ethan: For small models on Dedicated with optimized kernels we can get low 100s ms; hosted latency varies by model and region. we'll run a micro-benchmark for your 512-token case. 07:10 Priya: ok that would be helpful. also can you surface token-level cost in logs so we can attribute costs per feature? 07:18 Maya: yes Console gives token cost breakdown, and we can push usage events to your analytics pipeline. 07:25 Marco: about our gateway - we do JWT auth and some edge rate limiting. how would we best authenticate to Redwood? 07:33 Ethan: Use short-lived tokens or mTLS between your proxy and Redwood; Dedicated/Private support VPC peering and mTLS. for hosted we recommend API keys + IP allowlisting + signed headers through your proxy. 07:47 Alex: Any pitfalls you've seen with LangChain integrations? 07:50 Ethan: Most are around streaming compatibility and ensuring the retriever doesn't do n+1 calls; our examples show batching retriever calls and using prefix caching. 08:05 Maya: we'll share the sample repo and a small benchmark script that runs a typical LangChain pipeline with your retrieval size. 08:14 Priya: can the sample repo run in our CI? 08:17 Ethan: yes it's a small pytest harness and a docker compose that hits hosted endpoints; we can tweak it to point to Dedicated later. 08:26 Marco: about quotas - can we have burst windows, like bucket-based? 08:31 Ethan: Yes token-bucket style shaping is available and you can configure burst windows and per-tenant buckets. 08:40 Alex: operationally we'd want canary rollout for a new model. does Redwood support canary/A-B? 08:46 Maya: Redwood supports canary, A/B testing, and automatic fallback. rollouts can be configured per-route in Console. 08:54 Priya: who will be our main contact during POC? 08:58 Maya: I'll be your AE and Ethan will handle technical onboarding; we'll loop in a solutions engineer if we need infra touches. 09:05 Alex: ok good. any security docs now? 09:08 Maya: I'll send the security pack and SOC 2 report under NDA, plus our SAML docs. 09:14 Marco: we'd like a test that mirrors our gateway behavior. 09:18 Ethan: we'll include a sample proxy pattern and a small script you can run in your VPC to emulate burst traffic. 09:25 Alex: great. next steps recap? 09:27 Maya: we'll email pricing & comparison, security pack, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample + micro-benchmark, and propose POC schedule. 09:35 Priya: thanks, that works. 09:38 Alex: thanks everyone. 09:40 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up after the call with notes and links.
